keyVerseText: To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.
rootMeaning: The Greek word ἐνιαυτός (eniautós) is derived from a prolongation of the primary term ἔνος (énos), meaning 'a year.' This etymology highlights the concept of a complete cycle or anniversary of time, emphasizing not just a count of days but a full recurring period. The literal sense of ἐνιαυτός conveys the idea of a marked, repeating time-span, which enriches the common English translation 'year' by suggesting a cyclical or commemorative dimension.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐνιαυτός appears 14 times and is predominantly translated as 'year' or 'years,' indicating its consistent use to denote a defined period of time. The term is used both in singular and plural forms, sometimes referring to sabbatical years or specific cycles like the Pythagorean or Metonic cycles. This range shows that while the word generally means a year, it can also denote longer or more significant periods, underscoring the biblical emphasis on divinely appointed times and seasons.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐνιαυτός as a marked, cyclical period enriches our grasp of God's sovereign ordering of time in Scripture. It reminds believers that God governs history through appointed seasons and years, each carrying divine purpose and fulfillment. This concept underscores the faithfulness of God's timing in salvation history and encourages trust in His plans unfolding according to His perfect schedule. The use of this term in sacred texts points to the rhythm of divine revelation and covenantal faithfulness across generations.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 4:19, the phrase 'the acceptable year of the Lord' uses ἐνιαυτός to signify a special, divinely appointed time of favor and salvation. The word conveys more than a mere calendar year; it highlights a sacred season marked by God's grace and redemption. This enriches the verse by framing Jesus' mission as inaugurating a new era of God's mercy, inviting believers to embrace the timely and transformative work of the Lord.
